notes: Budgets for backend/runner/src/terminals/manager.ts: scripts/ratchet/ratchet.test.ts fails when the file grows past one, and a raise goes only as far as the file needs, never leaving headroom. Set from main at a1fbfdaf (2026-10-17).

slack is how far under its budget the file may sit before the budget must come down. A change that removes a little passes and the test prints the number the budget could be lowered to, so everyday product work never edits this file (about a third of main's commits touch manager.ts, and concurrent pull requests would conflict here). Past the slack, as after an extraction, the test fails until the budget is lowered (in a change that touches manager.ts or this file; any other change only prints it, as two changes merged one after the other can leave the file past a budget neither crossed alone), so a large win is locked in. Lowering a slack needs nothing; raising one is written as a raised budget is, with why and where from.

lines counts the file's lines. methods counts every function the Terminals class defines in its body: methods, accessors, the constructor and properties set to a function or arrow expression, read from its syntax tree, so formatting never moves it.

New behaviour goes in a sibling module under backend/runner/src/terminals/, as closes.ts, opens.ts and titles.ts do, with the class calling it. Work that can't is raised in the same pull request, written { "budget": n, "reason": "why", "from": "#PR or commit" }.

lines.reason: Transcript redaction: three Terminals options (transcriptMs, transcriptShutdownMs, redactor) with their Omit entries, the redactor's construction, the restart's save once the earlier screen is shown, and the restore's once its replay ends; the rest is in saving.ts. Transcript sealing: two more options (sealer, transcriptKeyMs) with their Omit entries and construction, and the restore's open before the shell starts, less the re-save once restored, which sealing makes redundant. Inbox turn rows (+3): Bindings and murmur reach Inbox and the redactor, so the redactor is a local shared with Saves, plus the Bindings host's turns entry. Interrupted-turn notice (+2): the restore reads the saved turn flag through restored(), its import and the call; the logic is in terminals/interrupted.ts. Windows resume (+1): the shell's prompt tells the sampler, which on Windows lets go of the agent a fresh shell resumes only a sample later; the logic is in terminals/sampling.ts. Peer reports (+1): TerminalPeers reads each terminal's latest tell and done from Inbox, as the agents listing shows them; the logic is in messaging/peers.ts. Standing done (+9): Inbox changes, delivered messages and the person's prompts republish the terminal's `reported` summary field through Bindings.publishReported; the rule is `standingDone` in messaging/peers.ts, the logic in terminals/binding/facts.ts. Inbox dismiss (+6, +2 methods): the router reaches Inbox only through Terminals, so dismissAsk and clearAsks forward to it; the logic is in messaging/inbox.ts. open_agent model and effort (+9): the models option (its doc, Omit entry, field, default and the Calls host's entry) carries each harness's model list to the open call, as install does; the checks are in terminals/calls.ts and the lookups in harnesses/service.ts. Close asks (+19): the router reaches the agents' asks to close a terminal through two Terminals methods (closeAsks, answerCloseAsk), as requests and answerRequest, with their field, host entry, imports, and release and shutdown calls; the logic is in terminals/closeasks.ts and calls.ts. Lead an existing agent (+6, +1 method): releaseLead is the router's entry to the person's release of a lead, and the Calls host takes the bindings; the logic is in terminals/leads.ts (closeAsks became approvals, in terminals/approvals.ts). Windows lead (+1): the Bindings host's pollMs entry, so a lead ends on Windows only a sample after its agent, as its resume does; the logic is in terminals/binding/facts.ts. Agent feedback (+12): the router reaches the in-memory drafts through a public `feedback` field, which takes its field, construction, the Calls host's entry, and the project-removal and shutdown calls; the logic is in messaging/feedback.ts. Unstarted worker restore (+3): the restore names the task a led worker lost before its agent's first session starts with again, and gives the record that task's doorbell nonce, as a startup command beside the resume's; the logic is in terminals/resumes.ts. Handle order (+3): the handleOrder option with its doc and Omit entry, which tests set to give handle words in list order; the logic is in terminals/handles.ts and names.ts. open_agent without a task, with a lead and a session to resume (+4): the Calls host takes the claims, and the create judges the session an agent asked to resume again and claims it once the shell runs it; the logic is in terminals/resumes.ts and calls.ts. harness-core split (+1): hookShellSlackMs is imported from @novadeck/harness-core/hook-command, where it moved, a second import line; no new code. Messaging split (+1): SendAnswer and AgentsAnswer are imported from messaging/sending.ts, where they moved, a second import line; no new code. Notes held across restarts (+1): Messaging's held option hands the notes a session holds to Reports.held, which keeps them with its AgentReport; the logic is in terminals/told.ts and binding/reports.ts. Grant environment checks (+1): the Approving host takes the environment a new terminal starts with, which the hooks' git and gh variables are compared against; the logic is in terminals/approving.ts and shell/permissions.ts.
